question: A company needs to store contract documents. A contract lasts for 5 years. During the 5-year period, the company must ensure that the documents cannot be overwritten or deleted. The company needs to encrypt the documents at rest and rotate the encryption keys automatically every year. Which combination of steps should a solutions architect take to meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead? (Choose two.)

choices.A: Store the documents in Amazon S3. Use S3 Object Lock in governance mode.
choices.B: Store the documents in Amazon S3. Use S3 Object Lock in compliance mode.
choices.C: Use server-side encryption with Amazon S3 managed encryption keys (SSE-S3). Configure key rotation.
choices.D: Use server-side encryption with AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) customer managed keys. Configure key rotation. E. Use server-side encryption with AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) customer provided (imported) keys. Configure key rotation.

explanation: B: Store the documents in Amazon S3. Use S3 Object Lock in compliance mode. D: Use server-side encryption with AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) customer managed keys. Configure key rotation.
key_word: rotate the encryption keys automatically every year

question: A company has a web application that is based on Java and PHP. The company plans to move the application from on premises to AWS. The company needs the ability to test new site features frequently. The company also needs a highly available and managed solution that requires minimum operational overhead. Which solution will meet these requirements?

choices.A: Create an Amazon S3 bucket. Enable static web hosting on the S3 bucket. Upload the static content to the S3 bucket. Use AWS Lambda to process all dynamic content.
choices.B: Deploy the web application to an AWS Elastic Beanstalk environment. Use URL swapping to switch between multiple Elastic Beanstalk environments for feature testing.
choices.C: Deploy the web application to Amazon EC2 instances that are configured with Java and PHP. Use Auto Scaling groups and an Application Load Balancer to manage the website’s availability.
choices.D: Containerize the web application. Deploy the web application to Amazon EC2 instances. Use the AWS Load Balancer Controller to dynamically route traffic between containers that contain the new site features for testing.

explanation: Deploy the web application to an AWS Elastic Beanstalk environment. Use URL swapping to switch between multiple Elastic Beanstalk environments for feature testing.

question: A company has an ordering application that stores customer information in Amazon RDS for MySQL. During regular business hours, employees run one-time queries for reporting purposes. Timeouts are occurring during order processing because the reporting queries are taking a long time to run. The company needs to eliminate the timeouts without preventing employees from performing queries. What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements?

choices.A: Create a read replica. Move reporting queries to the read replica.
choices.B: Create a read replica. Distribute the ordering application to the primary DB instance and the read replica.
choices.C: Migrate the ordering application to Amazon DynamoDB with on-demand capacity.
choices.D: Schedule the reporting queries for non-peak hours.

explanation: The timeouts happen because long reporting queries compete with transactional traffic on the same DB instance. A read replica provides an asynchronously replicated copy of the database that is ideal for read-only reporting, so moving those queries off the primary removes the contention without stopping employees from running them. Sending the order application itself to the replica does not help, because orders need writes and the replica is read-only. Moving to DynamoDB is a large re-architecture that is not justified by a reporting workload. Restricting reports to off-peak hours prevents employees from querying when they need to, which violates the requirement.
key_word: without preventing employees from performing queries
reporting queries are taking a long time
Timeouts are occurring during order processing

question: A hospital wants to create digital copies for its large collection of historical written records. The hospital will continue to add hundreds of new documents each day. The hospital’s data team will scan the documents and will upload the documents to the AWS Cloud. A solutions architect must implement a solution to analyze the documents, extract the medical information, and store the documents so that an application can run SQL queries on the data. The solution must maximize scalability and operational efficiency. Which combination of steps should the solutions architect take to meet these requirements? (Choose two.)

choices.A: Write the document information to an Amazon EC2 instance that runs a MySQL database.
choices.B: Write the document information to an Amazon S3 bucket. Use Amazon Athena to query the data.
choices.C: Create an Auto Scaling group of Amazon EC2 instances to run a custom application that processes the scanned files and extracts the medical information.
choices.D: Create an AWS Lambda function that runs when new documents are uploaded. Use Amazon Rekognition to convert the documents to raw text. Use Amazon Transcribe Medical to detect and extract relevant medical information from the text. E. Create an AWS Lambda function that runs when new documents are uploaded. Use Amazon Textract to convert the documents to raw text. Use Amazon Comprehend Medical to detect and extract relevant medical information from the text.

explanation: Two pieces are needed: an extraction pipeline for scanned documents and a queryable store. For extraction, Amazon Textract is the service that reads text from scanned images and forms, and Amazon Comprehend Medical is the NLP service that identifies medical entities in that text; wiring both into a Lambda function triggered on upload gives event-driven, serverless processing that scales with the daily volume. For storage, writing the results to S3 and querying with Athena gives standard SQL over the data with no servers to manage. Rekognition is for image and video analysis, not document OCR, and Transcribe Medical handles speech, not text. A self-managed MySQL on EC2 or an Auto Scaling fleet running custom parsing code adds operational burden and does not scale as efficiently.
key_word: run SQL queries on the data

question: A company is running a batch application on Amazon EC2 instances. The application consists of a backend with multiple Amazon RDS databases. The application is causing a high number of reads on the databases. A solutions architect must reduce the number of database reads while ensuring high availability. What should the solutions architect do to meet this requirement?

choices.A: Add Amazon RDS read replicas.
choices.B: Use Amazon ElastiCache for Redis.
choices.C: Use Amazon Route 53 DNS caching
choices.D: Use Amazon ElastiCache for Memcached.

explanation: The goal is to cut database reads, which points to caching frequently read results in front of the databases rather than adding more database capacity. Of the two ElastiCache engines, only Redis supports replication, Multi-AZ, and automatic failover, so it satisfies the high availability requirement; Memcached nodes hold data in a single node with no replication. Read replicas spread reads across more instances but every read still hits a database, so the total read count is not reduced. Route 53 caches DNS answers, which is unrelated to database query volume.
key_word: reduce the number of database reads

question: A company needs to run a critical application on AWS. The company needs to use Amazon EC2 for the application’s database. The database must be highly available and must fail over automatically if a disruptive event occurs. Which solution will meet these requirements?

choices.A: Launch two EC2 instances, each in a different Availability Zone in the same AWS Region. Install the database on both EC2 instances. Configure the EC2 instances as a cluster. Set up database replication.
choices.B: Launch an EC2 instance in an Availability Zone. Install the database on the EC2 instance. Use an Amazon Machine Image (AMI) to back up the data. Use AWS CloudFormation to automate provisioning of the EC2 instance if a disruptive event occurs.
choices.C: Launch two EC2 instances, each in a different AWS Region. Install the database on both EC2 instances. Set up database replication. Fail over the database to a second Region.
choices.D: Launch an EC2 instance in an Availability Zone. Install the database on the EC2 instance. Use an Amazon Machine Image (AMI) to back up the data. Use EC2 automatic recovery to recover the instance if a disruptive event occurs.

explanation: Automatic failover for a self-managed database on EC2 requires a second live instance that already has the data and can take over. Running two instances in different Availability Zones of the same Region, clustered together with replication between them, gives both fault isolation and immediate failover. Restoring from an AMI through CloudFormation or EC2 automatic recovery is a single-instance design: recovery takes time and the data on the AMI is only as fresh as the last backup, so it is neither highly available nor automatic in the required sense. Spreading the pair across two Regions adds latency to replication and typically needs a manual cross-Region failover, which is more than the question requires.
key_word: use Amazon EC2 for the application

question: A company’s order system sends requests from clients to Amazon EC2 instances. The EC2 instances process the orders and then store the orders in a database on Amazon RDS. Users report that they must reprocess orders when the system fails. The company wants a resilient solution that can process orders automatically if a system outage occurs. What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements?

choices.A: Move the EC2 instances into an Auto Scaling group. Create an Amazon EventBridge (Amazon CloudWatch Events) rule to target an Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) task.
choices.B: Move the EC2 instances into an Auto Scaling group behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB). Update the order system to send messages to the ALB endpoint.
choices.C: Move the EC2 instances into an Auto Scaling group. Configure the order system to send messages to an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue. Configure the EC2 instances to consume messages from the queue.
choices.D: Create an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic. Create an AWS Lambda function, and subscribe the function to the SNS topic. Configure the order system to send messages to the SNS topic. Send a command to the EC2 instances to process the messages by using AWS Systems Manager Run Command.

explanation: Orders are lost today because a request goes straight to an instance and disappears when that instance fails. Placing a durable queue between the clients and the processors decouples the two: each order is persisted in SQS until a consumer successfully deletes it, and if an instance fails mid-processing the message becomes visible again and another instance picks it up. An Auto Scaling group keeps enough consumers running. A load balancer only routes requests and holds nothing, so an in-flight order is still lost. Pushing through SNS to Lambda and then using Run Command to instruct instances is convoluted and SNS does not retain messages for later reprocessing.
key_word: process orders automatically if a system outage occurs
must reprocess orders when the system fails

question: A company runs an application on a large fleet of Amazon EC2 instances. The application reads and writes entries into an Amazon DynamoDB table. The size of the DynamoDB table continuously grows, but the application needs only data from the last 30 days. The company needs a solution that minimizes cost and development effort. Which solution meets these requirements?

choices.A: Use an AWS CloudFormation template to deploy the complete solution. Redeploy the CloudFormation stack every 30 days, and delete the original stack.
choices.B: Use an EC2 instance that runs a monitoring application from AWS Marketplace. Configure the monitoring application to use Amazon DynamoDB Streams to store the timestamp when a new item is created in the table. Use a script that runs on the EC2 instance to delete items that have a timestamp that is older than 30 days.
choices.C: Configure Amazon DynamoDB Streams to invoke an AWS Lambda function when a new item is created in the table. Configure the Lambda function to delete items in the table that are older than 30 days.
choices.D: Extend the application to add an attribute that has a value of the current timestamp plus 30 days to each new item that is created in the table. Configure DynamoDB to use the attribute as the TTL attribute.

explanation: DynamoDB has a built-in Time to Live feature: when an item carries an expiration timestamp in a designated attribute, the service deletes it automatically after that time at no additional cost and without consuming write capacity. Having the application stamp each new item with an expiry 30 days out and enabling TTL on that attribute is therefore the cheapest and simplest option. Deleting items from a Lambda function or an EC2 script consumes write capacity, requires scanning for old items, and adds code to maintain. Redeploying a whole stack every 30 days would destroy the table and all data in it, not just the old entries.
key_word: needs only data from the last 30 days

question: A company has a Microsoft .NET application that runs on an on-premises Windows Server. The application stores data by using an Oracle Database Standard Edition server. The company is planning a migration to AWS and wants to minimize development changes while moving the application. The AWS application environment should be highly available. Which combination of actions should the company take to meet these requirements? (Choose two.)

choices.A: Refactor the application as serverless with AWS Lambda functions running .NET Core.
choices.B: Rehost the application in AWS Elastic Beanstalk with the .NET platform in a Multi-AZ deployment.
choices.C: Replatform the application to run on Amazon EC2 with the Amazon Linux Amazon Machine Image (AMI).
choices.D: Use AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) to migrate from the Oracle database to Amazon DynamoDB in a Multi-AZ deployment. E. Use AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) to migrate from the Oracle database to Oracle on Amazon RDS in a Multi-AZ deployment.

explanation: Minimizing development changes means keeping the .NET application and the Oracle database engine as they are, while gaining high availability from managed services. Elastic Beanstalk has a native Windows .NET platform and can run the application across multiple Availability Zones behind a load balancer, so the code moves largely unchanged. Keeping Oracle on Amazon RDS with Multi-AZ provides synchronous standby and automatic failover for the database, and DMS handles the data transfer. Rewriting for Lambda or switching to DynamoDB would require significant code and data model changes. Moving to Amazon Linux is a replatform that a Windows .NET application cannot simply undergo.

question: A company runs a containerized application on a Kubernetes cluster in an on-premises data center. The company is using a MongoDB database for data storage. The company wants to migrate some of these environments to AWS, but no code changes or deployment method changes are possible at this time. The company needs a solution that minimizes operational overhead. Which solution meets these requirements?

choices.A: Use Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) with Amazon EC2 worker nodes for compute and MongoDB on EC2 for data storage.
choices.B: Use Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) with AWS Fargate for compute and Amazon DynamoDB for data storage
choices.C: Use Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) with Amazon EC2 worker nodes for compute and Amazon DynamoDB for data storage.
choices.D: Use Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) with AWS Fargate for compute and Amazon DocumentDB (with MongoDB compatibility) for data storage.

explanation: With no code or deployment changes allowed, the workloads must still run as Kubernetes deployments and still talk to a MongoDB-compatible database. Amazon EKS keeps the existing Kubernetes manifests and tooling working, and running pods on Fargate removes the need to manage worker nodes. Amazon DocumentDB speaks the MongoDB wire protocol, so the application connects as before while AWS handles patching, backups, and scaling of the database. Moving to ECS would change the deployment method, and switching to DynamoDB would require rewriting data access code. Running MongoDB on EC2 keeps the database operational burden on the company.
key_word: no code changes or deployment method changes

question: A telemarketing company is designing its customer call center functionality on AWS. The company needs a solution that provides multiple speaker recognition and generates transcript files. The company wants to query the transcript files to analyze the business patterns. The transcript files must be stored for 7 years for auditing purposes. Which solution will meet these requirements?

choices.A: Use Amazon Rekognition for multiple speaker recognition. Store the transcript files in Amazon S3. Use machine learning models for transcript file analysis.
choices.B: Use Amazon Transcribe for multiple speaker recognition. Use Amazon Athena for transcript file analysis.
choices.C: Use Amazon Translate for multiple speaker recognition. Store the transcript files in Amazon Redshift. Use SQL queries for transcript file analysis.
choices.D: Use Amazon Rekognition for multiple speaker recognition. Store the transcript files in Amazon S3. Use Amazon Textract for transcript file analysis.

explanation: The task combines speech-to-text with speaker identification, followed by ad hoc analysis of the resulting text files. Amazon Transcribe is the service that converts audio to text and includes speaker diarization, which labels which speaker said each segment. Its output lands naturally in S3, where Athena can run SQL over the transcripts without loading them anywhere, and S3 storage classes and lifecycle rules cover the 7-year retention cheaply. Rekognition works on images and video, not audio, and Translate converts text between languages. Textract extracts text from scanned documents, which is not what call recordings require.

question: A company hosts its application on AWS. The company uses Amazon Cognito to manage users. When users log in to the application, the application fetches required data from Amazon DynamoDB by using a REST API that is hosted in Amazon API Gateway. The company wants an AWS managed solution that will control access to the REST API to reduce development efforts. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

choices.A: Configure an AWS Lambda function to be an authorizer in API Gateway to validate which user made the request.
choices.B: For each user, create and assign an API key that must be sent with each request. Validate the key by using an AWS Lambda function.
choices.C: Send the user’s email address in the header with every request. Invoke an AWS Lambda function to validate that the user with that email address has proper access.
choices.D: Configure an Amazon Cognito user pool authorizer in API Gateway to allow Amazon Cognito to validate each request.

explanation: API Gateway has a native integration with Cognito user pools: an authorizer of that type validates the JSON Web Token in each request against the user pool with no custom code, so the application only needs to pass the token it already receives at login. That is a fully managed control with essentially no development effort. A Lambda authorizer could validate the same token, but the company would have to write and maintain that function. API keys identify calling applications for usage plans and are not an authentication mechanism for individual users. Trusting an email address sent in a header is insecure because any client could spoof it.
key_word: control access to the REST API

question: A company is developing a marketing communications service that targets mobile app users. The company needs to send confirmation messages with Short Message Service (SMS) to its users. The users must be able to reply to the SMS messages. The company must store the responses for a year for analysis. What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements?

choices.B: Build an Amazon Pinpoint journey. Configure Amazon Pinpoint to send events to an Amazon Kinesis data stream for analysis and archiving.

choices.D: Create an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) FIFO topic. Subscribe an Amazon Kinesis data stream to the SNS topic for analysis and archiving.

question: A company is planning to move its data to an Amazon S3 bucket. The data must be encrypted when it is stored in the S3 bucket. Additionally, the encryption key must be automatically rotated every year. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

choices.B: Create an AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) customer managed key. Enable automatic key rotation. Set the S3 bucket’s default encryption behavior to use the customer managed KMS key. Move the data to the S3 bucket.
choices.C: Create an AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) customer managed key. Set the S3 bucket’s default encryption behavior to use the customer managed KMS key. Move the data to the S3 bucket. Manually rotate the KMS key every year.
choices.D: Encrypt the data with customer key material before moving the data to the S3 bucket. Create an AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) key without key material. Import the customer key material into the KMS key. Enable automatic key rotation.

explanation: Create an AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) customer managed key. Enable automatic key rotation. Set the S3 bucket's default encryption behavior to use the customer managed KMS key. Move the data to the S3 bucket.

question: A company hosts a marketing website in an on-premises data center. The website consists of static documents and runs on a single server. choices.D: Create a public Amazon S3 bucket. Configure AWS Transfer for SFTP. Configure the S3 bucket for website hosting. Upload website content by using the SFTP client.

question: A company wants to manage Amazon Machine Images (AMIs). The company currently copies AMIs to the same AWS Region where the AMIs were created. choices.A: Create an AWS Lambda function to query AWS CloudTrail logs and to send an alert when a CreateImage API call is detected.
choices.B: Configure AWS CloudTrail with an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) notification that occurs when updated logs are sent to Amazon S3. Use Amazon Athena to create a new table and to query on CreateImage when an API call is detected.
choices.C: Create an Amazon EventBridge (Amazon CloudWatch Events) rule for the CreateImage API call. Configure the target as an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic to send an alert when a CreateImage API call is detected.
choices.D: Configure an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) FIFO queue as a target for AWS CloudTrail logs. Create an AWS Lambda function to send an alert to an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic when a CreateImage API call is detected.

explanation: Create an Amazon EventBridge (Amazon CloudWatch Events) rule for the CreateImage API call. Configure the target as an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic to send an alert when a CreateImage API call is detected.

question: A company owns an asynchronous API that is used to ingest user requests and, based on the request type, dispatch requests to the appropriate microservice for processing. The company is using Amazon API Gateway to deploy the API front end, and an AWS Lambda function that invokes Amazon DynamoDB to store user requests before dispatching them to the processing microservices. The company provisioned as much DynamoDB throughput as its budget allows, but the company is still experiencing availability issues and is losing user requests. What should a solutions architect do to address this issue without impacting existing users?

choices.A: Add throttling on the API Gateway with server-side throttling limits.
choices.B: Use DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) and Lambda to buffer writes to DynamoDB.
choices.C: Create a secondary index in DynamoDB for the table with the user requests.
choices.D: Use the Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue and Lambda to buffer writes to DynamoDB.

explanation: Requests are being lost because write bursts exceed what the DynamoDB table can absorb, and the budget prevents raising its throughput further. The fix is to decouple ingestion from the database write by placing a durable queue in the path: the API accepts the request and places it in SQS immediately, and a Lambda consumer drains the queue at a rate the table can handle. No request is dropped and callers see no change in behaviour. Adding server-side throttling on API Gateway would reject requests, which impacts users. DAX is a read-through cache and does not buffer writes. A secondary index increases write cost rather than relieving it.
key_word: as much DynamoDB throughput as its budget allows

question: A company needs to move data from an Amazon EC2 instance to an Amazon S3 bucket. The company must ensure that no API calls and no data are routed through public internet routes. choices.C: Run the nslookup tool from inside the EC2 instance to obtain the private IP address of the S3 bucket’s service API endpoint. Create a route in the VPC route table to provide the EC2 instance with access to the S3 bucket. Attach a resource policy to the S3 bucket to only allow the EC2 instance’s IAM role for access.
choices.D: Use the AWS provided, publicly available ip-ranges.json file to obtain the private IP address of the S3 bucket’s service API endpoint. Create a route in the VPC route table to provide the EC2 instance with access to the S3 bucket. Attach a resource policy to the S3 bucket to only allow the EC2 instance’s IAM role for access.

explanation: Create an interface VPC endpoint for Amazon S3 in the subnet where the EC2 instance is located. Attach a resource policy to the S3 bucket to only allow the EC2 instance's IAM role for access.
key_word: no API calls and no data

choices.C: Use Session Manager from AWS Systems Manager to manage the session.
choices.D: Use the GetSessionToken API operation in AWS Security Token Service (AWS STS) to manage the session.

question: A company offers a food delivery service that is growing rapidly. Because of the growth, the company’s order processing system is experiencing scaling problems during peak traffic hours. The current architecture includes the following: • A group of Amazon EC2 instances that run in an Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling group to collect orders from the application • Another group of EC2 instances that run in an Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling group to fulfill orders The order collection process occurs quickly, but the order fulfillment process can take longer. Data must not be lost because of a scaling event. A solutions architect must ensure that the order collection process and the order fulfillment process can both scale properly during peak traffic hours. The solution must optimize utilization of the company’s AWS resources. Which solution meets these requirements?

choices.A: Use Amazon CloudWatch metrics to monitor the CPU of each instance in the Auto Scaling groups. Configure each Auto Scaling group’s minimum capacity according to peak workload values.
choices.B: Use Amazon CloudWatch metrics to monitor the CPU of each instance in the Auto Scaling groups. Configure a CloudWatch alarm to invoke an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic that creates additional Auto Scaling groups on demand.
choices.C: Provision two Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queues: one for order collection and another for order fulfillment. Configure the EC2 instances to poll their respective queue. Scale the Auto Scaling groups based on notifications that the queues send.
choices.D: Provision two Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queues: one for order collection and another for order fulfillment. Configure the EC2 instances to poll their respective queue. Create a metric based on a backlog per instance calculation. Scale the Auto Scaling groups based on this metric.

explanation: Two queues decouple the fast collection step from the slower fulfillment step, so a scaling event cannot lose an order because every order is persisted in SQS until it is processed. The remaining question is how to scale the consumer fleets efficiently. The recommended approach is a custom metric that divides the number of messages waiting in the queue by the number of running instances, which yields a backlog-per-instance figure that target tracking can keep at a desired value. That scales each group in proportion to its actual work, optimizing utilization. SQS does not push scaling notifications to Auto Scaling, so scaling on queue notifications is not a real mechanism. CPU-based scaling and fixed minimum capacity either over-provision for peak or scale on a signal that does not reflect queue depth.
key_word: Data must not be lost because of a scaling event
order fulfillment process can take longer
scale properly during peak traffic hours

question: A company has a serverless website with millions of objects in an Amazon S3 bucket. The company uses the S3 bucket as the origin for an Amazon CloudFront distribution. question: A company runs a global web application on Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer. The application stores data in Amazon Aurora. The company needs to create a disaster recovery solution and can tolerate up to 30 minutes of downtime and potential data loss. The solution does not need to handle the load when the primary infrastructure is healthy. What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements?

choices.A: Deploy the application with the required infrastructure elements in place. Use Amazon Route 53 to configure active-passive failover. Create an Aurora Replica in a second AWS Region.
choices.B: Host a scaled-down deployment of the application in a second AWS Region. Use Amazon Route 53 to configure active-active failover. Create an Aurora Replica in the second Region.
choices.C: Replicate the primary infrastructure in a second AWS Region. Use Amazon Route 53 to configure active-active failover. Create an Aurora database that is restored from the latest snapshot.
choices.D: Back up data with AWS Backup. Use the backup to create the required infrastructure in a second AWS Region. Use Amazon Route 53 to configure active-passive failover. Create an Aurora second primary instance in the second Region.

explanation: Deploy the application with the required infrastructure elements in place. Use Amazon Route 53 to configure active-passive failover. Create an Aurora Replica in a second AWS Region.
key_word: 30 minutes of downtime and potential data loss
does not need to handle the load

question: A company has a web server running on an Amazon EC2 instance in a public subnet with an Elastic IP address. The default security group is assigned to the EC2 instance. The default network ACL has been modified to block all traffic. A solutions architect needs to make the web server accessible from everywhere on port 443. question: A company’s application is having performance issues. The application is stateful and needs to complete in-memory tasks on Amazon EC2 instances. The company used AWS CloudFormation to deploy infrastructure and used the M5 EC2 instance family. As traffic increased, the application performance degraded. Users are reporting delays when the users attempt to access the application. Which solution will resolve these issues in the MOST operationally efficient way?

choices.A: Replace the EC2 instances with T3 EC2 instances that run in an Auto Scaling group. Make the changes by using the AWS Management Console.
choices.B: Modify the CloudFormation templates to run the EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group. Increase the desired capacity and the maximum capacity of the Auto Scaling group manually when an increase is necessary.
choices.C: Modify the CloudFormation templates. Replace the EC2 instances with R5 EC2 instances. Use Amazon CloudWatch built-in EC2 memory metrics to track the application performance for future capacity planning.
choices.D: Modify the CloudFormation templates. Replace the EC2 instances with R5 EC2 instances. Deploy the Amazon CloudWatch agent on the EC2 instances to generate custom application latency metrics for future capacity planning.

explanation: Update the CloudFormation template to use a memory-optimized EC2 instance family instead of M5.

question: A solutions architect is designing a new API using Amazon API Gateway that will receive requests from users. The volume of requests is highly variable; several hours can pass without receiving a single request. choices.B: An AWS Lambda function
choices.C: A containerized service hosted in Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS)
choices.D: A containerized service hosted in Amazon ECS with Amazon EC2

explanation: An AWS Lambda function. Lambda supports asynchronous invocation and you only pay for the compute time consumed during code execution.

question: A company runs an application on a group of Amazon Linux EC2 instances. For compliance reasons, the company must retain all application log files for 7 years. choices.A: Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS)
choices.B: Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS)
choices.C: Amazon EC2 instance store
choices.D: Amazon S3

question: A company has hired an external vendor to perform work in the company’s AWS account. The vendor uses an automated tool that is hosted in an AWS account that the vendor owns. The vendor does not have IAM access to the company’s AWS account. How should a solutions architect grant this access to the vendor?

choices.A: Create an IAM role in the company’s account to delegate access to the vendor’s IAM role. Attach the appropriate IAM policies to the role for the permissions that the vendor requires.
choices.B: Create an IAM user in the company’s account with a password that meets the password complexity requirements. Attach the appropriate IAM policies to the user for the permissions that the vendor requires.
choices.C: Create an IAM group in the company’s account. Add the tool’s IAM user from the vendor account to the group. Attach the appropriate IAM policies to the group for the permissions that the vendor requires.
choices.D: Create a new identity provider by choosing “AWS account” as the provider type in the IAM console. Supply the vendor’s AWS account ID and user name. Attach the appropriate IAM policies to the new provider for the permissions that the vendor requires.

explanation: Create an IAM role in the company's account to delegate access to the vendor's IAM role. Attach the appropriate IAM policies to the role for the permissions that the vendor requires.
key_word: vendor does not have IAM access
hosted in an AWS account that the vendor owns

question: A company has deployed a Java Spring Boot application as a pod that runs on Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) in private subnets. The application needs to write data to an Amazon DynamoDB table. A solutions architect must ensure that the application can interact with the DynamoDB table without exposing traffic to the internet. Which combination of steps should the solutions architect take to accomplish this goal? (Choose two.)

choices.B: Attach an IAM user that has sufficient privileges to the EKS pod.
choices.C: Allow outbound connectivity to the DynamoDB table through the private subnets’ network ACLs.
choices.D: Create a VPC endpoint for DynamoDB. E. Embed the access keys in the Java Spring Boot code.

explanation: A: Attach an IAM role that has sufficient privileges to the EKS pod. D: Create a VPC endpoint for DynamoDB.

write data to an Amazon DynamoDB table

question: A company recently migrated its web application to AWS by rehosting the application on Amazon EC2 instances in a single AWS Region. The company wants to redesign its application architecture to be highly available and fault tolerant. Traffic must reach all running EC2 instances randomly. Which combination of steps should the company take to meet these requirements? (Choose two.)

choices.A: Create an Amazon Route 53 failover routing policy.
choices.B: Create an Amazon Route 53 weighted routing policy.
choices.C: Create an Amazon Route 53 multivalue answer routing policy.
choices.D: Launch three EC2 instances: two instances in one Availability Zone and one instance in another Availability Zone. E. Launch four EC2 instances: two instances in one Availability Zone and two instances in another Availability Zone.

explanation: High availability requires instances in more than one Availability Zone, and fault tolerance means the loss of a zone should not remove capacity in an unbalanced way. Placing an equal number of instances in each of two zones keeps the application balanced if one zone fails. For DNS, a multivalue answer routing policy returns up to eight healthy IP addresses in random order and uses health checks to drop unhealthy ones, which satisfies the requirement that traffic reach all running instances randomly. A failover policy sends traffic to a single primary and only switches on failure, and a weighted policy distributes by fixed proportions rather than randomly across all healthy targets. An odd split of instances leaves one zone with less capacity.
key_word: reach all running EC2 instances randomly

question: A media company collects and analyzes user activity data on premises. The company wants to migrate this capability to AWS. The user activity data store will continue to grow and will be petabytes in size. The company needs to build a highly available data ingestion solution that facilitates on-demand analytics of existing data and new data with SQL. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

choices.A: Send activity data to an Amazon Kinesis data stream. Configure the stream to deliver the data to an Amazon S3 bucket.
choices.B: Send activity data to an Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose delivery stream. Configure the stream to deliver the data to an Amazon Redshift cluster.
choices.C: Place activity data in an Amazon S3 bucket. Configure Amazon S3 to run an AWS Lambda function on the data as the data arrives in the S3 bucket.
choices.D: Create an ingestion service on Amazon EC2 instances that are spread across multiple Availability Zones. Configure the service to forward data to an Amazon RDS Multi-AZ database.

explanation: Send activity data to an Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose delivery stream. Configure the stream to deliver the data to an Amazon Redshift cluster.

question: A company collects data from thousands of remote devices by using a RESTful web services application that runs on an Amazon EC2 instance. The EC2 instance receives the raw data, transforms the raw data, and stores all the data in an Amazon S3 bucket. The number of remote devices will increase into the millions soon. choices.A: Use AWS Glue to process the raw data in Amazon S3.
choices.B: Use Amazon Route 53 to route traffic to different EC2 instances.
choices.C: Add more EC2 instances to accommodate the increasing amount of incoming data.
choices.D: Send the raw data to Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS). Use EC2 instances to process the data. E. Use Amazon API Gateway to send the raw data to an Amazon Kinesis data stream. Configure Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose to use the data stream as a source to deliver the data to Amazon S3.

question: A company needs to retain its AWS CloudTrail logs for 3 years. The company is enforcing CloudTrail across a set of AWS accounts by using AWS Organizations from the parent account. The CloudTrail target S3 bucket is configured with S3 Versioning enabled. An S3 Lifecycle policy is in place to delete current objects after 3 years. After the fourth year of use of the S3 bucket, the S3 bucket metrics show that the number of objects has continued to rise. However, the number of new CloudTrail logs that are delivered to the S3 bucket has remained consistent. Which solution will delete objects that are older than 3 years in the MOST cost-effective manner?

choices.A: Configure the organization’s centralized CloudTrail trail to expire objects after 3 years.
choices.B: Configure the S3 Lifecycle policy to delete previous versions as well as current versions.
choices.C: Create an AWS Lambda function to enumerate and delete objects from Amazon S3 that are older than 3 years.
choices.D: Configure the parent account as the owner of all objects that are delivered to the S3 bucket.

question: A company has an API that receives real-time data from a fleet of monitoring devices. The API stores this data in an Amazon RDS DB instance for later analysis. The amount of data that the monitoring devices send to the API fluctuates. During periods of heavy traffic, the API often returns timeout errors. choices.B: Modify the DB instance to be a Multi-AZ DB instance. Configure the application to write to all active RDS DB instances.
choices.C: Modify the API to write incoming data to an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue. Use an AWS Lambda function that Amazon SQS invokes to write data from the queue to the database.
choices.D: Modify the API to write incoming data to an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic. Use an AWS Lambda function that Amazon SNS invokes to write data from the topic to the database.

explanation: Modify the API to write incoming data to an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue. Use an AWS Lambda function that Amazon SQS invokes to write data from the queue to the database.

data is not lost during periods of heavy traffic

question: A company manages its own Amazon EC2 instances that run MySQL databases. The company is manually managing replication and scaling as demand increases or decreases. The company needs a new solution that simplifies the process of adding or removing compute capacity to or from its database tier as needed. choices.A: Migrate the databases to Amazon Aurora Serverless for Aurora MySQL.
choices.B: Migrate the databases to Amazon Aurora Serverless for Aurora PostgreSQL.
choices.C: Combine the databases into one larger MySQL database. Run the larger database on larger EC2 instances.
choices.D: Create an EC2 Auto Scaling group for the database tier. Migrate the existing databases to the new environment.

question: A company is concerned that two NAT instances in use will no longer be able to support the traffic needed for the company’s application. A solutions architect wants to implement a solution that is highly available, fault tolerant, and automatically scalable. What should the solutions architect recommend?

choices.C: Remove the two NAT instances and replace them with two NAT gateways in different Availability Zones.

question: An application runs on an Amazon EC2 instance that has an Elastic IP address in VPC

question: A company is building a new web-based customer relationship management application. choices.C: Use AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) to encrypt the EBS volumes and Aurora database storage at rest. Attach an AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) certificate to the ALB to encrypt data in transit.
choices.D: Use BitLocker to encrypt all data at rest. Import the company’s TLS certificate keys to AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) Attach the KMS keys to the ALB to encrypt data in transit.

explanation: Use AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) to encrypt the EBS volumes and Aurora database storage at rest. Attach an AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) certificate to the ALB to encrypt data in transit.

question: A company is moving its on-premises Oracle database to Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL. The database has several applications that write to the same tables. The applications need to be migrated one by one with a month in between each migration. Management has expressed concerns that the database has a high number of reads and writes. The data must be kept in sync across both databases throughout the migration. What should a solutions architect recommend?

choices.A: Use AWS DataSync for the initial migration. Use AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) to create a change data capture (CDC) replication task and a table mapping to select all tables.
choices.B: Use AWS DataSync for the initial migration. Use AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) to create a full load plus change data capture (CDC) replication task and a table mapping to select all tables.
choices.C: Use the AWS Schema Conversion Tool with AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) using a memory optimized replication instance. Create a full load plus change data capture (CDC) replication task and a table mapping to select all tables.
choices.D: Use the AWS Schema Conversion Tool with AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) using a compute optimized replication instance. Create a full load plus change data capture (CDC) replication task and a table mapping to select the largest tables.

explanation: Moving from Oracle to Aurora PostgreSQL is a heterogeneous migration, so the schema must first be converted with the AWS Schema Conversion Tool before DMS moves data. Because applications keep writing to both sides for several months, the DMS task must perform an initial full load and then continue capturing changes so the two databases stay in sync, and it must cover all tables rather than only the largest ones. Change data capture on a busy database is memory intensive, so a memory-optimized replication instance is the appropriate choice. DataSync is a file transfer service and cannot perform the initial load of a relational database.
key_word: Oracle database to Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL
kept in sync across both databases
high number of reads and writes
one by one with a month in between

choices.D: Use AWS Cost and Usage Reports to create a report with hourly granularity. Integrate the report data with Amazon Athena. Use Amazon EventBridge to schedule an Athena query. question: A solutions architect needs to design a new microservice for a company’s application. Clients must be able to call an HTTPS endpoint to reach the microservice. choices.D: Create an Amazon CloudFront distribution. Deploy the function to CloudFront Functions. Specify AWS_IAM as the authentication type.

question: A company previously migrated its data warehouse solution to AWS. The company also has an AWS Direct Connect connection. Corporate office users query the data warehouse using a visualization tool. choices.B: Host the visualization tool in the same AWS Region as the data warehouse. Access it over the internet.
choices.A: Host the visualization tool on premises and query the data warehouse directly over the internet.

question: An online learning company is migrating to the AWS Cloud. The company maintains its student records in a PostgreSQL database. question: A company hosts its web application on AWS using seven Amazon EC2 instances. The company requires that the IP addresses of all healthy EC2 instances be returned in response to DNS queries. Which policy should be used to meet this requirement?

question: A medical research lab produces data that is related to a new study. choices.B: Migrate the files to each clinic’s on-premises applications by using AWS DataSync for processing.
choices.C: Deploy an AWS Storage Gateway volume gateway as a virtual machine (VM) on premises at each clinic.

question: A company is using a content management system that runs on a single Amazon EC2 instance. The EC2 instance contains both the web server and the database software. choices.D: Move the database to a separate EC2 instance, and schedule backups to Amazon S3. Create an Amazon Machine Image (AMI) from the original EC2 instance. question: A company is launching an application on AWS. The application uses an Application Load Balancer (ALB) to direct traffic to at least two Amazon EC2 instances in a single target group. question: A company has deployed a database in Amazon RDS for MySQL. Due to increased transactions, the database support team is reporting slow reads against the DB instance and recommends adding a read replica. Which combination of actions should a solutions architect take before implementing this change? (Choose two.)

choices.A: Enable binlog replication on the RDS primary node.
choices.B: Choose a failover priority for the source DB instance.
choices.C: Allow long-running transactions to complete on the source DB instance.
choices.D: Create a global table and specify the AWS Regions where the table will be available. E. Enable automatic backups on the source instance by setting the backup retention period to a value other than 0.

explanation: Creating a read replica on RDS for MySQL has two prerequisites. The source must have automated backups enabled, because RDS uses the backup mechanism and binary logs to seed the replica; a retention period of 0 disables backups and blocks replica creation. In addition, long-running transactions should be allowed to finish first, since creating the replica takes a snapshot and active transactions can delay the process or cause replication lag. Binlog replication is managed by RDS itself and does not need to be enabled manually. Failover priority applies to Aurora replicas, not RDS for MySQL. Global tables are a DynamoDB concept and do not apply here.

question: A company is building a solution that will report Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling events across all the applications in an AWS account. The company needs to use a serverless solution to store the EC2 Auto Scaling status data in Amazon S3. The company then will use the data in Amazon S3 to provide near-real-time updates in a dashboard. The solution must not affect the speed of EC2 instance launches. How should the company move the data to Amazon S3 to meet these requirements?

choices.A: Use an Amazon CloudWatch metric stream to send the EC2 Auto Scaling status data to Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose. Store the data in Amazon S3.
choices.B: Launch an Amazon EMR cluster to collect the EC2 Auto Scaling status data and send the data to Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose. Store the data in Amazon S3.
choices.C: Create an Amazon EventBridge rule to invoke an AWS Lambda function on a schedule. Configure the Lambda function to send the EC2 Auto Scaling status data directly to Amazon S3.
choices.D: Use a bootstrap script during the launch of an EC2 instance to install Amazon Kinesis Agent. Configure Kinesis Agent to collect the EC2 Auto Scaling status data and send the data to Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose. Store the data in Amazon S3.

explanation: Auto Scaling publishes group metrics to CloudWatch, and a CloudWatch metric stream can push those metrics continuously to Kinesis Data Firehose, which batches and writes them to S3. The whole path is serverless, near real time, and completely outside the instance launch process, so it cannot slow launches down. An EMR cluster is a managed Hadoop environment and would be a heavyweight, non-serverless collector. Invoking Lambda on a schedule introduces polling delay and is not near real time. Installing an agent through a bootstrap script adds work to every launch, which directly conflicts with the requirement not to affect launch speed.
key_word: not affect the speed of EC2 instance launches

question: A company runs an application on Amazon EC2 instances. The company needs to implement a disaster recovery (DR) solution for the application. The DR solution needs to have a recovery time objective (RTO) of less than 4 hours. The DR solution also needs to use the fewest possible AWS resources during normal operations. Which solution will meet these requirements in the MOST operationally efficient way?

choices.A: Create Amazon Machine Images (AMIs) to back up the EC2 instances. Copy the AMIs to a secondary AWS Region. Automate infrastructure deployment in the secondary Region by using AWS Lambda and custom scripts.
choices.B: Create Amazon Machine Images (AMIs) to back up the EC2 instances. Copy the AMIs to a secondary AWS Region. Automate infrastructure deployment in the secondary Region by using AWS CloudFormation.
choices.C: Launch EC2 instances in a secondary AWS Region. Keep the EC2 instances in the secondary Region active at all times.
choices.D: Launch EC2 instances in a secondary Availability Zone. Keep the EC2 instances in the secondary Availability Zone active at all times.

explanation: Create Amazon Machine Images (AMIs) to back up the EC2 instances. Copy the AMIs to a secondary AWS Region. Automate infrastructure deployment in the secondary Region by using AWS CloudFormation.

question: A company runs an internal browser-based application. The application runs on Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer. The instances run in an Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling group across multiple Availability Zones. The Auto Scaling group scales up to 20 instances during work hours, but scales down to 2 instances overnight. Staff are complaining that the application is very slow when the day begins, although it runs well by mid-morning. How should the scaling be changed to address the staff complaints and keep costs to a minimum?

choices.A: Implement a scheduled action that sets the desired capacity to 20 shortly before the office opens.
choices.B: Implement a step scaling action triggered at a lower CPU threshold, and decrease the cooldown period.
choices.C: Implement a target tracking action triggered at a lower CPU threshold, and decrease the cooldown period.
choices.D: Implement a scheduled action that sets the minimum and maximum capacity to 20 shortly before the office opens.

explanation: Implement a target tracking action triggered at a lower CPU threshold, and decrease the cooldown period.
key_word: very slow when the day begins

question: A company has a multi-tier application deployed on several Amazon EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group. An Amazon RDS for Oracle instance is the application’ s data layer that uses Oracle-specific PL/SQL functions. Traffic to the application has been steadily increasing. This is causing the EC2 instances to become overloaded and the RDS instance to run out of storage. The Auto Scaling group does not have any scaling metrics and defines the minimum healthy instance count only. The company predicts that traffic will continue to increase at a steady but unpredictable rate before leveling off. What should a solutions architect do to ensure the system can automatically scale for the increased traffic? (Choose two.)

choices.A: Configure storage Auto Scaling on the RDS for Oracle instance.
choices.B: Migrate the database to Amazon Aurora to use Auto Scaling storage.
choices.C: Configure an alarm on the RDS for Oracle instance for low free storage space.
choices.D: Configure the Auto Scaling group to use the average CPU as the scaling metric. E. Configure the Auto Scaling group to use the average free memory as the scaling metric.

key_word: does not have any scaling metrics

question: A company provides an online service for posting video content and transcoding it for use by any mobile platform. The application architecture uses Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) Standard to collect and store the videos so that multiple Amazon EC2 Linux instances can access the video content for processing. As the popularity of the service has grown over time, the storage costs have become too expensive. Which storage solution is MOST cost-effective?

choices.B: Use AWS Storage Gateway for volumes to store and process the video content.
choices.C: Use Amazon EFS for storing the video content. Once processing is complete, transfer the files to Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS).
choices.D: Use Amazon S3 for storing the video content. Move the files temporarily over to an Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volume attached to the server for processing.

explanation: Use Amazon S3 for storing the video content. Move the files temporarily over to an Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volume attached to the server for processing.

Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) Standard

question: A company wants to create an application to store employee data in a hierarchical structured relationship. The company also needs to receive monthly email messages if any financial information is present in the employee data. Which combination of steps should a solutions architect take to meet these requirements? (Choose two.)

choices.A: Use Amazon Redshift to store the employee data in hierarchies. Unload the data to Amazon S3 every month.

choices.D: Use Amazon Athena to analyze the employee data in Amazon S3. Integrate Athena with Amazon QuickSight to publish analysis dashboards and share the dashboards with users. E. Configure Amazon Macie for the AWS account. Integrate Macie with Amazon EventBridge to send monthly notifications through an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) subscription.

explanation: B: Use Amazon DynamoDB to store the employee data in hierarchies. Export the data to Amazon S3 every month. E: Configure Amazon Macie for the AWS account. Integrate Macie with Amazon EventBridge to send monthly notifications through an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) subscription.

question: A company has an application that is backed by an Amazon DynamoDB table. The company’s compliance requirements specify that database backups must be taken every month, must be available for 6 months, and must be retained for 7 years. Which solution will meet these requirements?

choices.A: Create an AWS Backup plan to back up the DynamoDB table on the first day of each month. Specify a lifecycle policy that transitions the backup to cold storage after 6 months. Set the retention period for each backup to 7 years.
choices.B: Create a DynamoDB on-demand backup of the DynamoDB table on the first day of each month. Transition the backup to Amazon S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval after 6 months. Create an S3 Lifecycle policy to delete backups that are older than 7 years.
choices.C: Use the AWS SDK to develop a script that creates an on-demand backup of the DynamoDB table. Set up an Amazon EventBridge rule that runs the script on the first day of each month. Create a second script that will run on the second day of each month to transition DynamoDB backups that are older than 6 months to cold storage and to delete backups that are older than 7 years.
choices.D: Use the AWS CLI to create an on-demand backup of the DynamoDB table. Set up an Amazon EventBridge rule that runs the command on the first day of each month with a cron expression. Specify in the command to transition the backups to cold storage after 6 months and to delete the backups after 7 years.

explanation: Create an AWS Backup plan to back up the DynamoDB table on the first day of each month. Specify a lifecycle policy that transitions the backup to cold storage after 6 months. Set the retention period for each backup to 7 years.
key_word: backups must be taken every month

question: A company is using Amazon CloudFront with its website. The company has enabled logging on the CloudFront distribution, and logs are saved in one of the company’s Amazon S3 buckets. choices.B: Use standard SQL queries in Amazon Athena to analyze the CloudFront logs in the S3 bucket. Visualize the results with Amazon QuickSight.
choices.C: Use standard SQL queries in Amazon DynamoDB to analyze the CloudFront logs in the S3 bucket. Visualize the results with AWS Glue.
choices.D: Use standard SQL queries in Amazon DynamoDB to analyze the CloudFront logs in the S3 bucket. Visualize the results with Amazon QuickSight.

question: A company runs a fleet of web servers using an Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL DB instance. After a routine compliance check, the company sets a standard that requires a recovery point objective (RPO) of less than 1 second for all its production databases. Which solution meets these requirements?

choices.A: Enable a Multi-AZ deployment for the DB instance.
choices.B: Enable auto scaling for the DB instance in one Availability Zone.
choices.C: Configure the DB instance in one Availability Zone, and create multiple read replicas in a separate Availability Zone.
choices.D: Configure the DB instance in one Availability Zone, and configure AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) change data capture (CDC) tasks.

explanation: Enable a Multi-AZ deployment for the DB instance. In a Multi-AZ deployment, Amazon RDS automatically provisions and maintains a synchronous standby replica in a different Availability Zone.

question: A company runs a web application that is deployed on Amazon EC2 instances in the private subnet of a VP

choices.C: Move the EC2 instances into the public subnet. Give the EC2 instances a set of Elastic IP addresses.

question: A research company runs experiments that are powered by a simulation application and a visualization application. The simulation application runs on Linux and outputs intermediate data to an NFS share every 5 minutes. The visualization application is a Windows desktop application that displays the simulation output and requires an SMB file system. The company maintains two synchronized file systems. This strategy is causing data duplication and inefficient resource usage. The company needs to migrate the applications to AWS without making code changes to either application. Which solution will meet these requirements?

choices.A: Migrate both applications to AWS Lambda. Create an Amazon S3 bucket to exchange data between the applications.
choices.B: Migrate both applications to Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS). Configure Amazon FSx File Gateway for storage.
choices.C: Migrate the simulation application to Linux Amazon EC2 instances. Migrate the visualization application to Windows EC2 instances. Configure Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) to exchange data between the applications.
choices.D: Migrate the simulation application to Linux Amazon EC2 instances. Migrate the visualization application to Windows EC2 instances. Configure Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP for storage.

explanation: The core problem is that one application writes over NFS while the other reads over SMB, and the company currently keeps two copies in sync. A single file system that serves the same data through both protocols removes the duplication. Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP supports multi-protocol access, so a Linux EC2 instance can mount it over NFS and a Windows EC2 instance can map it over SMB, with no code changes to either application. Lambda cannot host a long-running Linux simulation or a Windows desktop application. FSx File Gateway is for on-premises access to FSx, not for in-cloud workloads on ECS. SQS passes messages, not files, and would require changing how both applications exchange data.

question: As part of budget planning, management wants a report of AWS billed items listed by user. The data will be used to create department budgets. A solutions architect needs to determine the most efficient way to obtain this report information. Which solution meets these requirements?

choices.A: Run a query with Amazon Athena to generate the report.
choices.B: Create a report in Cost Explorer and download the report.
choices.C: Access the bill details from the billing dashboard and download the bill.
choices.D: Modify a cost budget in AWS Budgets to alert with Amazon Simple Email Service (Amazon SES).

explanation: Create a report in Cost Explorer and download the report. AWS Cost Explorer allows you to visualize, understand, and manage your AWS costs and usage over time.
key_word: AWS billed items listed by user

question: A company hosts its static website by using Amazon S3. The company wants to add a contact form to its webpage. The contact form will have dynamic server-side components for users to input their name, email address, phone number, and user message. The company anticipates that there will be fewer than 100 site visits each month. Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

choices.A: Host a dynamic contact form page in Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS). Set up Amazon Simple Email Service (Amazon SES) to connect to any third-party email provider.
choices.B: Create an Amazon API Gateway endpoint with an AWS Lambda backend that makes a call to Amazon Simple Email Service (Amazon SES).
choices.C: Convert the static webpage to dynamic by deploying Amazon Lightsail. Use client-side scripting to build the contact form. Integrate the form with Amazon WorkMail.
choices.D: Create a t2.micro Amazon EC2 instance. Deploy a LAMP (Linux, Apache, MySQL, PHP/Perl/Python) stack to host the webpage. Use client- side scripting to build the contact form. Integrate the form with Amazon WorkMail.

explanation: Create an Amazon API Gateway endpoint with an AWS Lambda backend that makes a call to Amazon Simple Email Service (Amazon SES). This serverless architecture eliminates the need for managing infrastructure and costs are based on actual usage.
key_word: fewer than 100 site visits each month

question: A company has a static website that is hosted on Amazon CloudFront in front of Amazon S3. The static website uses a database backend. The company notices that the website does not reflect updates that have been made in the website’s Git repository. The company checks the continuous integration and continuous delivery (CI/CD) pipeline between the Git repository and Amazon S3. The company verifies that the webhooks are configured properly and that the CI/CD pipeline is sending messages that indicate successful deployments. A solutions architect needs to implement a solution that displays the updates on the website. Which solution will meet these requirements?

choices.A: Add an Application Load Balancer.
choices.B: Add Amazon ElastiCache for Redis or Memcached to the database layer of the web application.
choices.C: Invalidate the CloudFront cache.
choices.D: Use AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) to validate the website’s SSL certificate.

explanation: Invalidate the CloudFront cache. CloudFront caches content to improve performance; invalidating the cache forces CloudFront to re-fetch the latest content from the origin.

sending messages that indicate successful deployments

question: A company wants to migrate a Windows-based application from on premises to the AWS Cloud. The application has three tiers: an application tier, a business tier, and a database tier with Microsoft SQL Server. How should a solutions architect design the architecture to meet these requirements?

choices.A: Host all three tiers on Amazon EC2 instances. Use Amazon FSx File Gateway for file sharing between the tiers.
choices.B: Host all three tiers on Amazon EC2 instances. Use Amazon FSx for Windows File Server for file sharing between the tiers.
choices.C: Host the application tier and the business tier on Amazon EC2 instances. Host the database tier on Amazon RDS. Use Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) for file sharing between the tiers.
choices.D: Host the application tier and the business tier on Amazon EC2 instances. Host the database tier on Amazon RDS. Use a Provisioned IOPS SSD (io2) Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volume for file sharing between the tiers.

share files for processing between the tiers

question: A company is migrating a Linux-based web server group to AWS. The web servers must access files in a shared file store for some content. The company must not make any changes to the application. What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements?

choices.A: Create an Amazon S3 Standard bucket with access to the web servers.
choices.B: Configure an Amazon CloudFront distribution with an Amazon S3 bucket as the origin.

choices.D: Configure a General Purpose SSD (gp3) Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volume. Mount the EBS volume to all web servers.

question: A company has an AWS Lambda function that needs read access to an Amazon S3 bucket that is located in the same AWS account. Which solution will meet these requirements in the MOST secure manner?

choices.A: Apply an S3 bucket policy that grants read access to the S3 bucket.
choices.B: Apply an IAM role to the Lambda function. Apply an IAM policy to the role to grant read access to the S3 bucket.
choices.C: Embed an access key and a secret key in the Lambda function’s code to grant the required IAM permissions for read access to the S3 bucket.
choices.D: Apply an IAM role to the Lambda function. Apply an IAM policy to the role to grant read access to all S3 buckets in the account.

explanation: Apply an IAM role to the Lambda function. Apply an IAM policy to the role to grant read access to the S3 bucket. This follows the principle of least privilege and avoids persistent credentials.

question: A company hosts a web application on multiple Amazon EC2 instances. The EC2 instances are in an Auto Scaling group that scales in response to user demand. choices.B: On-Demand Instances only

choices.D: A mix of On-Demand Instances and Reserved Instances

question: A media company uses Amazon CloudFront for its publicly available streaming video content. question: A company is preparing a new data platform that will ingest real-time streaming data from multiple sources. The company needs to transform the data before writing the data to Amazon S3. Use AWS Glue to transform the data and to write the data to Amazon S3. Use Amazon Athena to query the transformed data.

question: A company has an on-premises volume backup solution that has reached its end of life. choices.D: Use AWS Storage Gateway and configure a stored volume gateway. Run the Storage Gateway software appliance on premises and map the gateway storage volumes to on-premises storage. Mount the gateway storage volumes to provide local access to the data.

question: An application that is hosted on Amazon EC2 instances needs to access an Amazon S3 bucket. Traffic must not traverse the internet. How should a solutions architect configure access to meet these requirements?

choices.B: Set up a gateway VPC endpoint for Amazon S3 in the VPC.
choices.C: Configure the EC2 instances to use a NAT gateway to access the S3 bucket.
choices.D: Establish an AWS Site-to-Site VPN connection between the VPC and the S3 bucket.

question: An ecommerce company stores terabytes of customer data in the AWS Cloud. The data contains personally identifiable information (PII). choices.B: Store the data in an Amazon S3 bucket. Process and transform the data by using S3 Object Lambda before returning the data to the requesting application.

choices.D: Process the data and store the transformed data in three separate Amazon DynamoDB tables so that each application has its own custom dataset. Point each application to its respective DynamoDB table.

question: A company deploys an application on five Amazon EC2 instances. An Application Load Balancer (ALB) distributes traffic to the instances by using a target group. A solutions architect needs to implement a solution to automate the scalability of the application. The solution must optimize the cost of the architecture and must ensure that the application has enough CPU resources when surges occur. Which solution will meet these requirements?

choices.A: Create an Amazon CloudWatch alarm that enters the ALARM state when the CPUUtilization metric is less than 20%. Create an AWS Lambda function that the CloudWatch alarm invokes to terminate one of the EC2 instances in the ALB target group.
choices.B: Create an EC2 Auto Scaling group. Select the existing ALB as the load balancer and the existing target group as the target group. Set a target tracking scaling policy that is based on the ASGAverageCPUUtilization metric. Set the minimum instances to 2, the desired capacity to 3, the maximum instances to 6, and the target value to 50%. Add the EC2 instances to the Auto Scaling group.
choices.C: Create an EC2 Auto Scaling group. Select the existing ALB as the load balancer and the existing target group as the target group. Set the minimum instances to 2, the desired capacity to 3, and the maximum instances to 6. Add the EC2 instances to the Auto Scaling group.
choices.D: Create two Amazon CloudWatch alarms. Configure the first CloudWatch alarm to enter the ALARM state when the average CPUUtilization metric is below 20%. Configure the second CloudWatch alarm to enter the ALARM state when the average CPUUtilization matric is above 50%. Configure the alarms to publish to an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic to send an email message. After receiving the message, log in to decrease or increase the number of EC2 instances that are running.

explanation: Create an EC2 Auto Scaling group. Select the existing ALB as the load balancer and the existing target group as the target group. Set a target tracking scaling policy that is based on the ASGAverageCPUUtilization metric. Set the minimum instances to 2, the desired capacity to 3, the maximum instances to 6, and the target value to 50%.

enough CPU resources when surges occur

question: A company is running a critical business application on Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer. The EC2 instances run in an Auto Scaling group and access an Amazon RDS DB instance. The design did not pass an operational review because the EC2 instances and the DB instance are all located in a single Availability Zone. A solutions architect must update the design to use a second Availability Zone. Which solution will make the application highly available?

choices.A: Provision a subnet in each Availability Zone. Configure the Auto Scaling group to distribute the EC2 instances across both Availability Zones. Configure the DB instance with connections to each network.
choices.B: Provision two subnets that extend across both Availability Zones. Configure the Auto Scaling group to distribute the EC2 instances across both Availability Zones. Configure the DB instance with connections to each network.
choices.C: Provision a subnet in each Availability Zone. Configure the Auto Scaling group to distribute the EC2 instances across both Availability Zones. Configure the DB instance for Multi-AZ deployment.
choices.D: Provision a subnet that extends across both Availability Zones. Configure the Auto Scaling group to distribute the EC2 instances across both Availability Zones. Configure the DB instance for Multi-AZ deployment.

explanation: A subnet in a VPC always belongs to exactly one Availability Zone, so any option that stretches a subnet across two zones is not possible. The correct design creates a separate subnet in each zone, lets the Auto Scaling group place instances across both, and turns on Multi-AZ for the RDS instance so a synchronous standby exists in the second zone with automatic failover. Configuring a database with connections to each network is not a feature; the standby and failover come from the Multi-AZ setting.

question: A research laboratory needs to process approximately 8 TB of data. The laboratory requires sub-millisecond latencies and a minimum throughput of 6 GBps for the storage subsystem. Hundreds of Amazon EC2 instances that run Amazon Linux will distribute and process the data. Which solution will meet the performance requirements?

choices.A: Create an Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP file system. Sat each volume’ tiering policy to ALL. Import the raw data into the file system. Mount the fila system on the EC2 instances.
choices.B: Create an Amazon S3 bucket to store the raw data. Create an Amazon FSx for Lustre file system that uses persistent SSD storage. Select the option to import data from and export data to Amazon S3. Mount the file system on the EC2 instances.
choices.C: Create an Amazon S3 bucket to store the raw data. Create an Amazon FSx for Lustre file system that uses persistent HDD storage. Select the option to import data from and export data to Amazon S3. Mount the file system on the EC2 instances.
choices.D: Create an Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP file system. Set each volume’s tiering policy to NONE. Import the raw data into the file system. Mount the file system on the EC2 instances.

explanation: Create an Amazon S3 bucket to store the raw data. Create an Amazon FSx for Lustre file system that uses persistent SSD storage. Select the option to import data from and export data to Amazon S3. Mount the file system on the EC2 instances. Amazon FSx for Lustre provides sub-millisecond latencies and is designed for high-throughput workloads.

question: A company needs to migrate a legacy application from an on-premises data center to the AWS Cloud because of hardware capacity constraints. The application runs 24 hours a day, 7 days a week. The application’s database storage continues to grow over time. What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

choices.A: Migrate the application layer to Amazon EC2 Spot Instances. Migrate the data storage layer to Amazon S3.
choices.B: Migrate the application layer to Amazon EC2 Reserved Instances. Migrate the data storage layer to Amazon RDS On-Demand Instances.
choices.C: Migrate the application layer to Amazon EC2 Reserved Instances. Migrate the data storage layer to Amazon Aurora Reserved Instances.
choices.D: Migrate the application layer to Amazon EC2 On-Demand Instances. Migrate the data storage layer to Amazon RDS Reserved Instances.

explanation: Migrate the application layer to Amazon EC2 Reserved Instances. Migrate the data storage layer to Amazon Aurora Reserved Instances.

database storage continues to grow over time

question: A university research laboratory needs to migrate 30 TB of data from an on-premises Windows file server to Amazon FSx for Windows File Server. The laboratory has a 1 Gbps network link that many other departments in the university share. The laboratory wants to implement a data migration service that will maximize the performance of the data transfer. However, the laboratory needs to be able to control the amount of bandwidth that the service uses to minimize the impact on other departments. The data migration must take place within the next 5 days. Which AWS solution will meet these requirements?

choices.A: AWS Snowcone
choices.B: Amazon FSx File Gateway
choices.C: AWS DataSync
choices.D: AWS Transfer Family

explanation: AWS DataSync. DataSync is a fully managed data transfer service that can control bandwidth and is designed for high-speed data transfers.
key_word: maximize the performance of the data transfer

question: A company wants to create a mobile app that allows users to stream slow-motion video clips on their mobile devices. Currently, the app captures video clips and uploads the video clips in raw format into an Amazon S3 bucket. The app retrieves these video clips directly from the S3 bucket.
