The company also wants to scale the application automatically when application demand increases. The company will use AWS Elastic Beanstalk for application deployment. Which solution will meet these requirements?

choices.A: Configure an Elastic Beanstalk environment to use burstable performance instances in unlimited mode. Configure the environment to scale based on requests.
choices.B: Configure an Elastic Beanstalk environment to use compute optimized instances. Configure the environment to scale based on requests.
choices.C: Configure an Elastic Beanstalk environment to use compute optimized instances. Configure the environment to scale on a schedule.
choices.D: Configure an Elastic Beanstalk environment to use burstable performance instances in unlimited mode. Configure the environment to scale on predictive metrics.

explanation: Burstable instances handle CPU spikes cost-effectively. Request-based scaling matches demand. Compute-optimized instances (Option B) are overprovisioned for intermittent spikes.
key_word: immediately increases to 10 times its normal amount

question: A company has customers located across the world. The company wants to use automation to secure its systems and network infrastructure. The company's security team must be able to track and audit all incremental changes to the infrastructure. Which solution will meet these requirements?

choices.A: Use AWS Organizations to set up the infrastructure. Use AWS Config to track changes.
choices.B: Use AWS CloudFormation to set up the infrastructure. Use AWS Config to track changes.
choices.C: Use AWS Organizations to set up the infrastructure. Use AWS Service Catalog to track changes.
choices.D: Use AWS CloudFormation to set up the infrastructure. Use AWS Service Catalog to track changes.

explanation: CloudFormation automates infrastructure; Config tracks changes for auditing. Service Catalog (Options C/D) is for governance, not change tracking.
key_word: track and audit all incremental changes

question: A startup company is hosting a website for its customers on an Amazon EC2 instance. The website consists of a stateless Python application and a MySQL database. The website serves only a small amount of traffic. The company is concerned about the reliability of the instance and needs to migrate to a highly available architecture. The company cannot modify the application code. Which combination of actions should a solutions architect take to achieve high availability for the website? (Choose two.)

choices.A: Provision an internet gateway in each Availability Zone in use.
choices.B: Migrate the database to an Amazon RDS for MySQL Multi-AZ DB instance.
choices.C: Migrate the database to Amazon DynamoDB, and enable DynamoDB auto scaling.
choices.D: Use AWS DataSync to synchronize the database data across multiple EC2 instances. E. Create an Application Load Balancer to distribute traffic to an Auto Scaling group of EC2 instances that are distributed across two Availability Zones.

explanation: RDS Multi-AZ ensures DB high availability. ALB + Auto Scaling distributes traffic across AZs. DynamoDB (Option C) requires code changes; DataSync (Option D) doesn’t solve HA.
key_word: stateless Python application and a MySQL database

question: A company is moving its data and applications to AWS during a multiyear migration project. The company wants to securely access data on Amazon S3 from the company's AWS Region and from the company's on-premises location. The data must not traverse the internet. The company has established an AWS Direct Connect connection between its Region and its on-premises location. Which solution will meet these requirements?

choices.A: Create gateway endpoints for Amazon S3. Use the gateway endpoints to securely access the data from the Region and the on-premises location.
choices.B: Create a gateway in AWS Transit Gateway to access Amazon S3 securely from the Region and the on-premises location.
choices.C: Create interface endpoints for Amazon S3. Use the interface endpoints to securely access the data from the Region and the on-premises location.
choices.D: Use an AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) key to access the data securely from the Region and the on-premises location.

explanation: Gateway endpoints allow secure S3 access via Direct Connect/VPC without internet. Interface endpoints (Option C) are for private-link services, not S3.

question: A company created a new organization in AWS Organizations. The organization has multiple accounts for the company's development teams. The development team members use AWS IAM Identity Center (AWS Single Sign-On) to access the accounts. For each of the company's applications, the development teams must use a predefined application name to tag resources that are created. A solutions architect needs to design a solution that gives the development team the ability to create resources only if the application name tag has an approved value. Which solution will meet these requirements?

choices.A: Create an IAM group that has a conditional Allow policy that requires the application name tag to be specified for resources to be created.
choices.B: Create a cross-account role that has a Deny policy for any resource that has the application name tag.
choices.C: Create a resource group in AWS Resource Groups to validate that the tags are applied to all resources in all accounts.
choices.D: Create a tag policy in Organizations that has a list of allowed application names.

explanation: Tag policies enforce standardized tagging across accounts. IAM policies (Option A) cannot validate tag values.
key_word: application name tag has an approved value

question: A company runs its databases on Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL. The company wants a secure solution to manage the master user password by rotating the password every 30 days. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

choices.A: Use Amazon EventBridge to schedule a custom AWS Lambda function to rotate the password every 30 days.
choices.B: Use the modify-db-instance command in the AWS CLI to change the password.
choices.C: Integrate AWS Secrets Manager with Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL to automate password rotation.
choices.D: Integrate AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store with Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL to automate password rotation.

explanation: Secrets Manager automates rotation every 30 days with zero operational effort. Manual rotation (Option B) or Parameter Store (Option D) lacks automation.

question: A company performs tests on an application that uses an Amazon DynamoDB table. The tests run for 4 hours once a week. The company knows how many read and write operations the application performs to the table each second during the tests. The company does not currently use DynamoDB for any other use case. A solutions architect needs to optimize the costs for the table. Which solution will meet these requirements?

choices.A: Choose on-demand mode. Update the read and write capacity units appropriately.
choices.B: Choose provisioned mode. Update the read and write capacity units appropriately.
choices.C: Purchase DynamoDB reserved capacity for a 1-year term.
choices.D: Purchase DynamoDB reserved capacity for a 3-year term.

explanation: Provisioned mode is cost-effective for predictable weekly workloads. On-demand (Option A) is expensive for infrequent use.
key_word: knows how many read and write operations
optimize the costs for the table

question: A company runs its applications on Amazon EC2 instances. The company performs periodic financial assessments of its AWS costs. The company recently identified unusual spending. The company needs a solution to prevent unusual spending. The solution must monitor costs and notify responsible stakeholders in the event of unusual spending. Which solution will meet these requirements?

choices.A: Use an AWS Budgets template to create a zero spend budget.
choices.B: Create an AWS Cost Anomaly Detection monitor in the AWS Billing and Cost Management console.
choices.C: Create AWS Pricing Calculator estimates for the current running workload pricing details.
choices.D: Use Amazon CloudWatch to monitor costs and to identify unusual spending.

explanation: Automatically detects and alerts on unusual spending. CloudWatch (Option D) lacks built-in anomaly detection.

question: A marketing company receives a large amount of new clickstream data in Amazon S3 from a marketing campaign. The company needs to analyze the clickstream data in Amazon S3 quickly. Then the company needs to determine whether to process the data further in the data pipeline. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

choices.A: Create external tables in a Spark catalog. Configure jobs in AWS Glue to query the data.
choices.B: Configure an AWS Glue crawler to crawl the data. Configure Amazon Athena to query the data.
choices.C: Create external tables in a Hive metastore. Configure Spark jobs in Amazon EMR to query the data.
choices.D: Configure an AWS Glue crawler to crawl the data. Configure Amazon Kinesis Data Analytics to use SQL to query the data.

explanation: Glue catalogs data; Athena provides serverless SQL queries. EMR (Option C) adds operational overhead.
key_word: analyze the clickstream data in Amazon S3 quickly
determine whether to process the data further

question: A company runs an SMB file server in its data center. The file server stores large files that the company frequently accesses for up to 7 days after the file creation date. After 7 days, the company needs to be able to access the files with a maximum retrieval time of 24 hours. Which solution will meet these requirements?

choices.A: Use AWS DataSync to copy data that is older than 7 days from the SMB file server to AWS.
choices.B: Create an Amazon S3 File Gateway to increase the company's storage space. Create an S3 Lifecycle policy to transition the data to S3 Glacier Deep Archive after 7 days.
choices.C: Create an Amazon FSx File Gateway to increase the company's storage space. Create an Amazon S3 Lifecycle policy to transition the data after 7 days.
choices.D: Configure access to Amazon S3 for each user. Create an S3 Lifecycle policy to transition the data to S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval after 7 days.

explanation: File Gateway extends on-prem storage; Glacier Deep Archive is cost-effective for archives. DataSync (Option A) doesn’t automate tiering.
key_word: frequently accesses for up to 7 days

question: A company runs a web application on Amazon EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group. The application uses a database that runs on an Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL DB instance. The application performs slowly when traffic increases. The database experiences a heavy read load during periods of high traffic. Which actions should a solutions architect take to resolve these performance issues? (Choose two.)

choices.A: Turn on auto scaling for the DB instance.
choices.B: Create a read replica for the DB instance. Configure the application to send read traffic to the read replica.
choices.C: Convert the DB instance to a Multi-AZ DB instance deployment. Configure the application to send read traffic to the standby DB instance.
choices.D: Create an Amazon ElastiCache cluster. Configure the application to cache query results in the ElastiCache cluster. E. Configure the Auto Scaling group subnets to ensure that the EC2 instances are provisioned in the same Availability Zone as the DB instance.

explanation: Read replicas offload read traffic. ElastiCache reduces DB load. Multi-AZ (Option C) doesn’t scale reads; auto scaling (Option A) isn’t for RDS.
key_word: heavy read load during periods of high traffic

question: A company uses Amazon EC2 instances and Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volumes to run an application. The company creates one snapshot of each EBS volume every day to meet compliance requirements. The company wants to implement an architecture that prevents the accidental deletion of EBS volume snapshots. The solution must not change the administrative rights of the storage administrator user. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST administrative effort?

choices.A: Create an IAM role that has permission to delete snapshots. Attach the role to a new EC2 instance. Use the AWS CLI from the new EC2 instance to delete snapshots.
choices.B: Create an IAM policy that denies snapshot deletion. Attach the policy to the storage administrator user.
choices.C: Add tags to the snapshots. Create retention rules in Recycle Bin for EBS snapshots that have the tags.
choices.D: Lock the EBS snapshots to prevent deletion.

explanation: Prevents accidental deletion without IAM changes. Recycle Bin (Option C) requires tagging; IAM (Option B) changes permissions.
key_word: prevents the accidental deletion of EBS volume snapshots
must not change the administrative rights

question: A company's application uses Network Load Balancers, Auto Scaling groups, Amazon EC2 instances, and databases that are deployed in an Amazon VP

choices.C: Create a trail in AWS CloudTrail. Configure VPC Flow Logs to send the log data to the trail. Use Amazon Kinesis Data Streams to stream the logs from the trail to OpenSearch Service.
choices.A: Create a log group in Amazon CloudWatch Logs. Configure VPC Flow Logs to send the log data to the log group. Use Amazon Kinesis Data Streams to stream the logs from the log group to OpenSearch Service.
choices.B: Create a log group in Amazon CloudWatch Logs. Configure VPC Flow Logs to send the log data to the log group. Use Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose to stream the logs from the log group to OpenSearch Service.
choices.D: Create a trail in AWS CloudTrail. Configure VPC Flow Logs to send the log data to the trail. Use Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose to stream the logs from the trail to OpenSearch Service.

explanation: Flow Logs capture traffic; Firehose streams to OpenSearch. CloudTrail (Options C/D) logs API calls, not network traffic.

question: A company is developing an application that will run on a production Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) cluster. The EKS cluster has managed node groups that are provisioned with On-Demand Instances. The company needs a dedicated EKS cluster for development work. The company will use the development cluster infrequently to test the resiliency of the application. The EKS cluster must manage all the nodes. Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

choices.A: Create a managed node group that contains only Spot Instances.
choices.B: Create two managed node groups. Provision one node group with On-Demand Instances. Provision the second node group with Spot Instances.
choices.C: Create an Auto Scaling group that has a launch configuration that uses Spot Instances. Configure the user data to add the nodes to the EKS cluster.
choices.D: Create a managed node group that contains only On-Demand Instances.

explanation: Balances cost (Spot) and reliability (On-Demand) for infrequent dev workloads. All-Spot (Option A) risks interruptions; self-managed ASG (Option C) adds overhead.
key_word: test the resiliency of the application
EKS cluster must manage all the nodes

question: A company stores sensitive data in Amazon S3. A solutions architect needs to create an encryption solution. The company needs to fully control the ability of users to create, rotate, and disable encryption keys with minimal effort for any data that must be encrypted. Which solution will meet these requirements?

choices.A: Use default server-side encryption with Amazon S3 managed encryption keys (SSE-S3) to store the sensitive data.
choices.B: Create a customer managed key by using AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS). Use the new key to encrypt the S3 objects by using server-side encryption with AWS KMS keys (SSE-KMS).
choices.C: Create an AWS managed key by using AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS). Use the new key to encrypt the S3 objects by using server-side encryption with AWS KMS keys (SSE-KMS).
choices.D: Download S3 objects to an Amazon EC2 instance. Encrypt the objects by using customer managed keys. Upload the encrypted objects back into Amazon S3.

explanation: Grants full control over key rotation/access. SSE-S3 (Option A) lacks key management. Client-side encryption (Option D) is complex.
key_word: create, rotate, and disable encryption keys

question: A company wants to back up its on-premises virtual machines (VMs) to AWS. The company's backup solution exports on-premises backups to an Amazon S3 bucket as objects. The S3 backups must be retained for 30 days and must be automatically deleted after 30 days. Which combination of steps will meet these requirements? (Choose three.)

choices.A: Create an S3 bucket that has S3 Object Lock enabled.
choices.B: Create an S3 bucket that has object versioning enabled.
choices.C: Configure a default retention period of 30 days for the objects.
choices.D: Configure an S3 Lifecycle policy to protect the objects for 30 days. E. Configure an S3 Lifecycle policy to expire the objects after 30 days. F. Configure the backup solution to tag the objects with a 30-day retention period

explanation: Versioning + retention policies automate compliance. Lifecycle rules expire objects. Object Lock (Option A) prevents deletion; tagging (Option F) doesn’t enforce retention.

question: A solutions architect needs to copy files from an Amazon S3 bucket to an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) file system and another S3 bucket. The files must be copied continuously. New files are added to the original S3 bucket consistently. The copied files should be overwritten only if the source file changes. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

choices.A: Create an AWS DataSync location for both the destination S3 bucket and the EFS file system. Create a task for the destination S3 bucket and the EFS file system. Set the transfer mode to transfer only data that has changed.
choices.B: Create an AWS Lambda function. Mount the file system to the function. Set up an S3 event notification to invoke the function when files are created and changed in Amazon S3. Configure the function to copy files to the file system and the destination S3 bucket.
choices.C: Create an AWS DataSync location for both the destination S3 bucket and the EFS file system. Create a task for the destination S3 bucket and the EFS file system. Set the transfer mode to transfer all data.
choices.D: Launch an Amazon EC2 instance in the same VPC as the file system. Mount the file system. Create a script to routinely synchronize all objects that changed in the origin S3 bucket to the destination S3 bucket and the mounted file system.

explanation: Continuously syncs only modified files to S3/EFS. Lambda (Option B) requires custom code; full syncs (Option C) are inefficient.
key_word: overwritten only if the source file changes
file system and another S3 bucket

question: A company uses Amazon EC2 instances and stores data on Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volumes. The company must ensure that all data is encrypted at rest by using AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS). The company must be able to control rotation of the encryption keys. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

choices.A: Create a customer managed key. Use the key to encrypt the EBS volumes.
choices.B: Use an AWS managed key to encrypt the EBS volumes. Use the key to configure automatic key rotation.
choices.C: Create an external KMS key with imported key material. Use the key to encrypt the EBS volumes.
choices.D: Use an AWS owned key to encrypt the EBS volumes.

explanation: Allows control over key rotation. AWS-managed keys (Option B) limit rotation flexibility.
key_word: control rotation of the encryption keys

question: A company needs a solution to enforce data encryption at rest on Amazon EC2 instances. The solution must automatically identify noncompliant resources and enforce compliance policies on findings. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST administrative overhead?

choices.A: Use an IAM policy that allows users to create only encrypted Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volumes. Use AWS Config and AWS Systems Manager to automate the detection and remediation of unencrypted EBS volumes.
choices.B: Use AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) to manage access to encrypted Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volumes. Use AWS Lambda and Amazon EventBridge to automate the detection and remediation of unencrypted EBS volumes.
choices.C: Use Amazon Macie to detect unencrypted Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volumes. Use AWS Systems Manager Automation rules to automatically encrypt existing and new EBS volumes.
choices.D: Use Amazon inspector to detect unencrypted Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volumes. Use AWS Systems Manager Automation rules to automatically encrypt existing and new EBS volumes.

explanation: Config detects noncompliant volumes; Systems Manager automates remediation. Macie (Option C) is for data classification, not encryption.

question: A company is migrating its multi-tier on-premises application to AWS. The application consists of a single-node MySQL database and a multi-node web tier. The company must minimize changes to the application during the migration. The company wants to improve application resiliency after the migration. Which combination of steps will meet these requirements? (Choose two.)

choices.A: Migrate the web tier to Amazon EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group behind an Application Load Balancer.
choices.B: Migrate the database to Amazon EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group behind a Network Load Balancer.
choices.C: Migrate the database to an Amazon RDS Multi-AZ deployment.
choices.D: Migrate the web tier to an AWS Lambda function. E. Migrate the database to an Amazon DynamoDB table.

explanation: Auto Scaling improves web tier resiliency; RDS Multi-AZ ensures DB HA. Lambda (Option D) requires code changes; DynamoDB (Option E) is incompatible.

question: A company wants to migrate its web applications from on premises to AWS. The company is located close to the eu-central-1 Region. Because of regulations, the company cannot launch some of its applications in eu-central-1. The company wants to achieve single-digit millisecond latency. Which solution will meet these requirements?

choices.A: Deploy the applications in eu-central-1. Extend the company’s VPC from eu-central-1 to an edge location in Amazon CloudFront.
choices.B: Deploy the applications in AWS Local Zones by extending the company's VPC from eu-central-1 to the chosen Local Zone.
choices.C: Deploy the applications in eu-central-1. Extend the company’s VPC from eu-central-1 to the regional edge caches in Amazon CloudFront.
choices.D: Deploy the applications in AWS Wavelength Zones by extending the company’s VPC from eu-central-1 to the chosen Wavelength Zone.

explanation: Local Zones provide single-digit latency near eu-central-1 while complying with regulations. CloudFront (Option A) is for caching, not app hosting.
key_word: cannot launch some of its applications in eu-central-1
